newsitem.title: UK: Bass hit by Clarke's "alcopop" tax.
newsitem.headline: Bass hit by Clarke's "alcopop" tax.

text.p: Shares in brewer Bass Plc, makers of Britain's biggest selling alcoholic soft drink Hoopers Hooch, fell 13p to 810p on Tuesday after Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said from January 1, the tax on alcoholic soft drinks will be increased by over 40 percent.
That puts up the price per bottle by seven to eight pence, said Clarke in his budget statement.
Shares in Merrydown were off 4p at 98p.

"This will meet public concern about the attraction of these alcopops for under age drinkers but actually attack a distortion of competition by bringing the tax broadly in line with beer," said Clarke in his budget statement.
Hooper's Hooch and Merrydown owned Two Dogs brand were the first two competing brands to land on the alcopop market less than two years ago but now there are over 90 alcoholic soft drinks in Britain.
Hooper's Hooch has an estimated 70 percent market share.
A report by researchers Datamonitor published on Monday estimated that the market was set to double from 108 million stg in sales in 1995.

Some 65 percent of the UK alcoholic soft drinks volume is made up of alcoholic lemonades, largely due to Hooper's Hooch but future growth is expected to come from both alcoholic fruit carbonates, like orange or cherryade and also from alcoholic sodas.
Hooch itself is now available in blackcurrant and Two Dogs has a variant called Rhubarb Rhubarb.
Shares in cider maker Matthew Clark rose 7-1/2p to close at 308p. Rival cider-maker shares HP Bulmer gained 6p to finish at 532-1/2p.

Matthew Clark stunned the stock market in September with a profits warning that wiped more than 290 million stg off its market value. The company has been decimated by the unprecedented growth in alcopops in the summer and price competition.
Since September its shares have held up at about 60 perecnt below their pre-warning September 9 price of 670p.
